newsitem.title: USA: U.S. uncertain about potential salmon deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. uncertain about potential salmon deal.

text.p: The United States and Canada on Thursday held a second day of talks on dividing the Pacific salmon catch but it is too soon to say if there will be an agreement, the State Department said.
"It's too early to tell at this time about how they will end," spokesman John Dinger said.
He said the contentious talks, which opened on Wednesday in Vancouver, resumed on Thursday morning. Another round will be held on Friday, he said.

"We are negotiating in good faith. We are working very hard toward an agreement that our negotiator can take back to our stakeholders and hope that we can quickly and successfully conclude these talks," Dinger added.

The negotiations collapsed in acrimony on May 21 when the Canadians angrily walked out of the last talks in Seattle, saying the lead U.S. negotiator was not authorised to offer a specific catch reduction.

Canada suspended the negotiations and accused the United States of bargaining in bad faith. That prompted a war of words between the two countries and it took several weeks of diplomatic efforts to get negotiations back on track.
Canadian Fisheries Minister David Anderson has said the situation was more promising now because the lead U.S. negotiator, Mary Beth West, had a mandate to negotiate a compromise.
The two countries have squabbled for years over how to divide dwindling salmon stocks in the Pacific Northwest and several attempts at a settlement have failed.
But pressure is mounting for a deal soon as the salmon fishing season gets underway.
